newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin tells defence minister to stop whining.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin tells defence minister to stop whining.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday told Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, who has been pushing for more cash for the armed forces, to get down to work on military reform instead of "whining" in public.

"The President of the Russian Federation does not approve of remarks made by the defence minister on February 23," said a Kremlin statement, read to reporters by presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky.
"The president knows how difficult it is now for the people in epaulettes. But whining will not help matters, concrete actions are needed."
"Only military reform can radically improve the situation," said the statement. It said Rodionov and Yeltsin's top defence adviser, Yuri Baturin, should coordinate their positions.
The two defence officials have been squabbling increasingly openly over the course of military reform.
Baturin wants reforms carried out within government spending plans, but Rodionov has been campaigning to win more funding for the armed forces.
"If concrete steps are not taken in the near future -- by 2000 or thereabouts -- our country's defences will be in ruins," he told retired officers at the weekend.

Yeltsin told Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Monday that a cabinet reshuffle might help improve the situation in the country, news which triggered a wave of rumours over which ministers might be sacked.
The liberal newspaper Izvestia said it would be Chernomyrdin himself. Itar-Tass news agency on Wednesday singled out Rodionov and said he might be dismissed in March.
Yastrzhembsky said he did not know who might be fired in any government reshuffle.
"I have no information confirming that any dismissal is planned of anyone occupying an important post in the government," Yastrzhembsky said. "I think best of all would be to be patient and wait."
Yastrzhembsky said earlier this week that the reshuffle would not include Chernomyrdin. The stolid premier is viewed in financial markets as a guarantor of Russia's economic reform course.
